title: Multi-level Value Alignment in Agentic AI Systems: Survey and Perspectives

bias_targets.methodology: The paper surveys evaluation methods utilizing benchmark datasets (such as BBQ, CBBQ, and StereoSet) that employ multiple-choice questions, binary judgments, and ranking tasks to quantify stereotypical biases and prejudice in language model outputs.

The paper reviews methodologies for evaluating gender bias using specific datasets (like WinoBias, WinoGender, and WikiGenderBias), which utilize coreference resolution tasks, expert-driven binary judgments, and open-ended questions, particularly highlighting contexts like automated recruitment screening.

The paper surveys the evaluation of cultural value alignment and bias using datasets (such as CDEval, CultureSPA, and HofstedeCulturalDimensions) that rely on multiple-choice questions and hybrid generation approaches to measure how well models represent diverse cultural frameworks.

The paper discusses the theoretical presence of latent political and moral biases in large language models, surveying alignment methods like Multi-Task Pre-training and Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) to detect and mitigate these biases.
